description: Representing, generating, editing, analyzing and synthesizing audio. Audio objects hold sampled sound with metadata and work directly with the signal-processing functions, while Sound and SoundNote cover symbolic and musical sound.

tools.name: Audio
tools.description: Represents sampled audio, constructed from a file, URL, list of samples or a Sound object. It stores sample rate, channels and duration, and renders as an interactive player in a notebook. Nearly every audio function takes and returns Audio objects.
tools.example:
a = Audio[Table[Sin[2 Pi 440 t], {t, 0, 2, 1/22050}], SampleRate -> 22050];
Duration[a]
tools.notes: AudioData, AudioLength, AudioChannels and AudioSampleRate extract the underlying properties.

tools.name: AudioGenerator
tools.description: Synthesizes audio from a named model such as a sine tone, sawtooth, noise color or a pure function of time. Duration and sample rate are specified directly. Use it to produce test signals, tones and noise beds.
tools.usage:
AudioGenerator[model, dur]
AudioGenerator[{"Sin", f}, dur, SampleRate -> sr]

tools.name: AudioPlot
tools.description: Plots the waveform of an audio object against time, with one panel per channel. Standard plot options for range, labels and styling apply. Use it to inspect amplitude envelopes and clipping.
tools.example:
a = AudioGenerator[{"Sin", 5}, 1];
AudioPlot[a, Frame -> True, FrameLabel -> {"t (s)", "amplitude"}]

tools.name: AudioData
tools.description: Extracts the raw sample values of an audio object as a list of channels. A type argument selects the numeric representation. Use it when you need to drop out of the Audio framework into plain array computation.

tools.name: AudioLength
tools.description: Returns the number of samples per channel in an audio object. It is the sample-count counterpart of Duration, which returns seconds. Use it when indexing or partitioning sample data.

tools.name: AudioSampleRate
tools.description: Gives the sample rate of an audio object in samples per second. Knowing it is essential for converting between sample indices and seconds and for filter design. AudioResample changes it.

tools.name: AudioChannels
tools.description: Returns the number of channels in an audio object, such as 1 for mono and 2 for stereo. Use it before channel-specific processing. AudioChannelMix converts between channel layouts.

tools.name: AudioResample
tools.description: Changes the sample rate of an audio object, resampling the waveform with anti-aliasing. It is required when combining audio recorded at different rates. Resampling method can be selected.

tools.name: AudioTrim
tools.description: Extracts a time interval from an audio object, or automatically trims leading and trailing silence. Times can be given in seconds or as Quantity values. Use it to cut clips and remove dead air.

tools.name: AudioJoin
tools.description: Concatenates audio objects in sequence, resampling and channel-matching them as needed. It is the basic editing operation for assembling clips. Use AudioOverlay to mix rather than concatenate.

tools.name: AudioSplit
tools.description: Splits an audio object at given times or according to a detected criterion such as silence. The result is a list of audio segments. Use it to break recordings into utterances or events.

tools.name: AudioPartition
tools.description: Divides audio into fixed-length frames, optionally overlapping, returning a list of audio objects. Framing is the first step of nearly every audio feature-extraction pipeline. Offsets control the hop size.
tools.notes: AudioBlockMap applies a function to each frame and reassembles the result.

tools.name: AudioBlockMap
tools.description: Applies a function to successive blocks of audio samples and returns the mapped result, optionally as a TimeSeries. It is the standard way to compute frame-level features or apply block-based processing. Block size and offset are specified in seconds or samples.
tools.usage:
AudioBlockMap[f, audio, dur]
AudioBlockMap[f, audio, dur, offset]

tools.name: AudioNormalize
tools.description: Scales audio so that its peak or loudness reaches a target level. It prevents clipping and makes recordings comparable in level. A level specification can target peak amplitude or perceptual loudness.

tools.name: AudioAmplify
tools.description: Multiplies the amplitude of audio by a constant or a time-varying function. Values above one can clip, so combine with AudioNormalize when needed. Use it for gain staging and simple envelopes.

tools.name: AudioFade
tools.description: Applies fade-in and fade-out envelopes at the start and end of an audio object. Durations and fade shapes are configurable. Use it to avoid clicks when cutting or concatenating clips.

tools.name: AudioDelay
tools.description: Adds a delayed copy of the signal to itself, producing echo effects. Delay time, gain and number of repeats are controllable. Use it as a building block for reverb and spatial effects.
tools.notes: AudioReverb provides a full room-simulation effect.

tools.name: AudioReverb
tools.description: Applies a reverberation effect simulating a room, with control over reverb time, damping and dry/wet mix. It produces a much richer effect than a simple delay. Use it for spatialization of synthesized or dry recordings.

tools.name: AudioPitchShift
tools.description: Shifts the pitch of audio by a factor or a musical interval without changing its duration. It uses phase-vocoder style processing. Use it for transposition and voice modification.
tools.notes: AudioTimeStretch changes duration without changing pitch; AudioFrequencyShift shifts all frequencies by a constant offset instead of a ratio.

tools.name: AudioTimeStretch
tools.description: Changes the duration of audio by a factor while keeping the pitch unchanged. It is the complement of AudioPitchShift. Use it to fit audio to a target length or to slow down speech for analysis.

tools.name: AudioFrequencyShift
tools.description: Shifts every frequency component of the audio by a fixed offset in hertz, which changes harmonic relationships. Unlike pitch shifting it does not preserve the timbre of harmonic sounds. Use it for ring-modulation style effects and for moving a band out of an interference region.

tools.name: AudioChannelMix
tools.description: Converts audio between channel configurations, such as stereo to mono, or applies an explicit mixing matrix. It handles common layouts by name. Use it to standardize channel counts before analysis.

tools.name: AudioMeasurements
tools.description: Computes global or frame-level measurements of audio such as peak, RMS, loudness, crest factor, spectral centroid and MFCC. A list of properties returns several at once, and a partition specification gives them over time. It is the main feature-extraction entry point for audio machine learning.
tools.notes: AudioLocalMeasurements returns the same quantities as time series over the audio.

tools.name: AudioLocalMeasurements
tools.description: Computes audio features frame by frame and returns them as TimeSeries objects. This is the time-varying counterpart of AudioMeasurements. Use it to plot feature trajectories and to build sequence models.

tools.name: AudioDistance
tools.description: Measures the distance or dissimilarity between two audio objects using a chosen feature space and metric. It supports signal-level and perceptual comparisons. Use it for quality assessment and nearest-neighbour audio search.

tools.name: AudioIdentify
tools.description: Classifies the kind of sound present in an audio object, returning an Entity such as a musical instrument or environmental sound. It uses a pretrained neural network. Use it for quick sound tagging without training a model.

tools.name: AudioCapture
tools.description: Records audio from a connected input device, either for a fixed duration or as a live stream. It is the acquisition counterpart of CurrentImage for sound. Device and sample rate can be selected.
tools.notes: Requires a microphone and system permission; $AudioInputDevices lists available devices.

tools.name: AudioStream
tools.description: Creates a playback stream for an audio object that can be started, stopped and queried programmatically. It gives fine control over playback position and looping. Use it for interactive applications and long files.

tools.name: SpeechSynthesize
tools.description: Converts text into spoken audio using a system or cloud text-to-speech voice. Language and voice can be specified. Use it for spoken output, accessibility and audio dataset generation.
tools.notes: VoiceStyleData lists the voices available on the current system.

tools.name: SpeechRecognize
tools.description: Transcribes spoken audio into text, optionally returning word-level timings or an alignment. A recognition language can be specified. Use it for transcription, voice commands and subtitle generation.

tools.name: Sound
tools.description: Represents a symbolic sound built from primitives such as SoundNote and SampledSoundList. Unlike Audio it describes sound to be synthesized rather than stored samples. Use it for music notation and MIDI-style output.
tools.notes: Audio[sound] converts a symbolic Sound into sampled audio; Export to MIDI is supported.

tools.name: SoundNote
tools.description: Represents a musical note or chord with a pitch, duration and instrument. Pitches can be note names, MIDI numbers or None for rests. Use it inside Sound to build melodies and chord progressions.

tools.name: SampledSoundList
tools.description: Represents sound given as an explicit list of amplitude samples at a specified sample rate, for use inside Sound. It is the low-level sampled primitive of the symbolic sound system. For most work an Audio object is more convenient.

tools.name: Play
tools.description: Synthesizes sound from a mathematical function of time over a given interval. It is the audio analogue of Plot and is ideal for demonstrating waveforms and beats. Sample rate and play range are options.
tools.example: Play[Sin[2 Pi 440 t] + Sin[2 Pi 445 t], {t, 0, 3}]
tools.notes: AudioGenerator with a pure function gives the same result as an Audio object, which is more flexible for further processing.
